$comment: THE DEVICE-DETAILS VOCABULARY: one row per key a Canary's own answers use (its HTTP and Bluetooth answers, its MQTT publishes, its serial records) that a diagnostics dump must treat by class. Each row names its class and the firmware sources ('surfaces') that emit it as a JSON key; scripts/gen_device_vocabulary.py refuses a row a named surface does not emit, or that names none, so the vocabulary says what the devices say. The generator writes custom_components/securacv/device_vocabulary.py (HACS ships that directory alone, so the integration cannot read spec/), whose redacted keys diagnostics.py unions into TO_REDACT: a row added here in a redacted class is redacted with no edit to diagnostics.py. Seeded (sweep HA56) with the keys of ledger F391 that a firmware source emits; serial_number and chip_id, which F391 also named, are emitted by none and stay integration-owned in diagnostics.py until one does. This file is also the input the general identifier lint (ledger F430) is to read; that lint is not built. Edit here, run python3 scripts/gen_device_vocabulary.py, commit both; lint.yml runs --check. When firmware renames or drops a key a row names, Canaries on the earlier release still send the old one: add it to INTEGRATION_REDACT_KEYS in diagnostics.py, with the release that last sent it, before the row moves (the generator will not write a module that stops redacting a key the committed one redacts).

identifier.means: A value that names one unit, or one radio peer of it, for as long as it lasts. Posted in a dump, it lets a stranger match the device.

health_counter.means: A count or an age a Canary reports about itself. Together they can single a device out across dumps and hint at when it reboots or is busy.

keys.means: the AI module's id slot; since F384 the Vision sends 1 or 0 there (a module answered) and never the module's own id, and the key stays redacted so a build that sent the id would not reach a dump
a Bluetooth address: the connected peer's, or a scanned or paired device's
the Bluetooth address of the peer a pairing is with
how long the Canary has been up, in seconds
how many times the Canary has booted
how many writes the card has taken this boot
how many requests the web server has answered this boot
how long ago the radar's last frame arrived, in milliseconds
